observation.visible_scene: An outdoor bonfire built as a cone/teepee of long branches and logs, burning with a tall orange-yellow flame against a backdrop of pine and leafy trees, a green-roofed open shelter with stacked cut logs on the right, grass and bare ground, and a small white jug on the lower left. The sky is pale, suggesting dusk. The fire is already well established at the first frame.
visible_changes: The flame continuously flickers: its height, width, and lean change from frame to frame (e.g., a broader, right-leaning plume with a puff at the top around frames 10–12, a thinner column in several mid frames), while its base stays anchored at the top of the wood pile.
A faint smoke/steam plume rises above the flame tip and drifts/shifts in shape over the segment.
The wood pile itself (the arrangement of branches and logs) remains structurally unchanged in position and shape throughout the excerpt; no collapse or movement of individual logs is visible.
The background elements (trees, shelter, log stack, white jug) hold fixed screen positions across all frames, indicating no camera translation or zoom.
The overall brightness and color of the flame fluctuate slightly with the flicker but the fire persists without extinguishing.
outside_clip_unknowns: How and when the fire was lit, and what fuel or accelerant (if any) was used.
Whether the pile is consumed, collapses, or the flame grows/shrinks after the last frame.
The presence of wind or air currents that would explain the flame's lean.
Any human activity near the fire outside this cropped window.
uncertain_details: The exact cause of the flame's lateral lean and shape changes (air movement vs. fuel geometry) cannot be determined from the frames.
Minor pixel-level differences in the wood pile between frames are too small to confirm any real settling versus compression artifacts.
Whether the camera is perfectly static or has negligible handheld drift cannot be fully separated from the fixed background.
